articles.title: Low-Density 3D Point Cloud Classification
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.05291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: 3D point cloud classification, a task in computer vision, has recently gained substantial interest due to its extensive applications across various domains such as augmented and virtual reality, robotics, and autonomous driving. However, classifying 3D point clouds becomes challenging in real-world scenarios where the density levels vary. These variations are due to limitations inherent to current sensing technologies and variable environmental conditions, which often prevent the capture of detailed and comprehensive geometric representations. Existing classification methods, which have demonstrated impressive results on dense point clouds, may be affected and could experience reduced performance when dealing with low-density point clouds. Addressing this challenge, this paper introduces LD-PointNet++, an architecture optimized for the classification of low-density point clouds. To pave the way for LD-PointNet++, we conduct the first benchmarking study that systematically evaluates state-of-the-art point cloud classification methods across varying densities, revealing significant performance declines in low-density environments. Experimental results on the ModelNet benchmark dataset demonstrate that LD-PointNet++ not only outperforms these methods in low-density scenarios but also demonstrates consistent accuracy above 90% across different density levels.

articles.title: Wonder 4: A Mixture-of-Experts Recipe for Image Quality Enhancement
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.05294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A real photograph is often blurry, grainy, compressed, scratched, and low-resolution at the same time. Each defect has its own severity and its own place in the image. The corrections for these defects conflict with each other. Exist- ing models describe the whole image with one description, so they cannot say where each correction belongs. To solve this problem, we present Wonder 4, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model for image quality enhancement. It corrects several defects of a real photograph at the same time, each in the region where it occurs. Every block of the model holds a mixture of N = 13 experts. A router, trained with the model, sends every image patch to k = 5 of them. No degradation classifier, mask, prompt, detector, or task label is used. Another issue is that standard MoE training, taken from language models, pushes every expert toward equal use. Equal use applies every correction everywhere, even where it is not needed. We replace this rule with a bias that only sets a minimum share of use. Across all patches, an expert used less than this minimum gets higher router scores until it is selected again. An expert above the minimum is not changed, so no expert is forced to be used as often as the others. The bias needs no extra loss. The method adds no extra module and no extra processing step. We evaluate Wonder 4 on DIV2K and Flickr2K, against five published methods and three open-weight pipelines. It reaches the best LPIPS, DISTS, and NIQE on all three test settings (DIV2K x4, DIV2K x8, and Flickr2K x4).

articles.title: OpenBrain: An Auditable Generated-Label Release for Whole-Brain MRI Parcellation
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.05348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic tools can now generate whole-brain MRI parcellations at cohort scale, but generated-label releases often provide little evidence about which cases are reliable enough to reuse. We introduce OpenBrain, a confidence-aware release of 35,838 provenance-verified OpenNeuro T1w cases from 607 source datasets. OpenBrain is organized as an auditable case-record release rather than a directory of standalone segmentation files: each record links a primary parcellation, two committee parcellations, source/license provenance, raw QC-7 measurements, percentile risks, a combined risk score R, and a confidence tier. QC-7 is a reference-free reliability panel over label geometry, image-label consistency, and committee disagreement, so users can filter, weight, audit, or re-threshold generated labels without rerunning inference. We evaluate this released evidence under a frozen protocol. Across external cohorts, lower QC-7 risk corresponds to higher generated-label quality; in fixed-budget training, lower-risk selections improve paired macro Dice over random selection by +3.2 to +3.7 percentage points. OpenBrain also exposes raw axes, committee outputs, provenance, and datasheet documentation, so confidence claims remain inspectable after download. It does not turn generated labels into manual annotations or clinical-grade segmentations. Its contribution is a large open generated-parcellation substrate, a reusable case-level risk-evidence layer, and an external validation protocol for release-time QC. Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/lanqz7766/OpenBrain. Code: https://github.com/lanqz7766/openbrain.

articles.title: GSCV++: Lightweight 3D Gaussian Splatting Sequence Compression via Standard Video Codecs
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.05359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents GSCV++, a lightweight pipeline for 3D {G}aussian {S}platting (GS) sequences {C}ompression with standard {V}ideo codecs. To meet the requirements of low-complexity and hardware compatibility from the industry, GSCV++ jointly improves preprocessing, 3D-to-2D mapping, and practical video compression configuration of GS compression. First, for preprocessing, energy-adaptive inter-frame spherical harmonic (SH) alternative current (AC) dimensionality reduction (EA-SHDR) is proposed to produces a compact and stable temporal SH AC feature space. It can reduce the data volume of following mapping and practical compression, as well as less complexity while eliminating redundant information. Second, for 3D-to-2D mapping, prior-based Inter-MiniPLAS (P-MiniPLAS) is designed to generate smooth 2D feature maps through prior-based weighting factor inference and small scale remapping. Compared with vanilla Parallel Linear Assignment Sorting (PLAS) and Morton scan, P-MiniPLAS ensures the generated 2D maps are more suitable for the video codec while maintaining a low level of computational complexity. Third, for practical compression, content-aware generalized compression (CA-GC) is developed to use a non-uniform bit-depth split for coordinate map generation, and a coding unit size selection is introduced for efficient compression complexity control, which fully exploits the performance of video codecs without involving normative changes. Experiments demonstrate that GSCV++ reports over 20\% in intra- and 60\% in inter-prediction rate-distortion gains compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. articles.title: Visibility-Aware Reference Generation for Benchmarking Visual 3D Reconstruction in Vegetation-Rich Environments
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.05361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable evaluation of visual 3D reconstruction and depth estimation in vegetation-rich outdoor environments is limited by the scarcity of geometric ground-truth data and the cost of complete scanner surveys. We present a LiDARbased reference-generation pipeline for evaluating the zero-shot performance of feed-forward visual-geometry models alongside conventional structure-from-motion (SfM) methods. The pipeline reuses camera images, LiDAR scans, and reference poses from existing multi-sensor localization datasets to generate per-view depth maps and visible reference point clouds. To address visibility errors in accumulated LiDAR scans, we introduce the LargeDepth-Gap Visibility Score (LDGVS) for point-wise visibility filtering and automatic scale selection in Hidden Point Removal(HPR). Experiments on TartanAirV2 and TartanGround show that, compared with Poisson surface reconstruction, which is an approach suited to completed scan surveys, the combined HPR and LDGVS filtering retains approximately three times the point density at comparable absolute relative error. We also apply the pipeline to the BotanicGarden dataset to systematically compare depth estimation and 3D reconstruction methods. Feedforward methods produce dense depth predictions efficiently, but their 3D reconstructions can contain duplicated structures. Conventional SfM generally produces more coherent geometry, but its reconstructions remain sparse and more prone to failure in challenging vegetated scenes. The benchmark toolkit and datasets will be released.

articles.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.05377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner. Our approach extracts compact latent actions from the video model's rich spatiotemporal features, compressing each latent video frame by $\boldsymbol{300\times}$ ($\boldsymbol{1{,}200 \rightarrow 4}$ tokens). In addition, by leveraging the video model's generative prior, these latent actions capture action-relevant dynamics disentangled from visual appearance. The resulting latent space serves as a shared action interface across embodiments (human and robot), environments, and action parameterizations. On LARY-Bench, DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models. Moreover, actions encoded in one setting remain effective in another: the latent space supports any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer across diverse embodiments and environments. Furthermore, this shared interface also enables policy learning in a compact latent action space, reducing the computational cost of video-diffusion-based policies.

articles.title: CoReMatch: Recurrent Continuous Coordinate Refinement for Real-Time Robotic Feature Matching
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03932v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Feature matching underpins many robotic perception tasks, including visual localization, mapping, SLAM, and autonomous navigation. Existing semi-dense matchers predict confidence on fixed grids, limiting correspondences to predefined locations and requiring costly high-resolution grids for precise localization. We present CoReMatch (Coordinate Refinement Match), a recurrent framework that refines correspondences directly in continuous coordinate space rather than predicting discrete confidence maps. CoReMatch progressively improves correspondence estimates by propagating information across iterations. At the coarse stage, a Deep Aggregated Transformer captures global context and iteratively updates correspondence coordinates, while a lightweight regression head further sharpens their localization. Experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks show that CoReMatch strikes a strong balance between accuracy and efficiency, outperforming Efficient LoFTR in accuracy while running more than 10x faster on embedded edge hardware. These results demonstrate that recurrent coordinate refinement offers an efficient and scalable approach to real-time feature matching for robotic perception.

articles.title: A Novel Conditional Adversarial Diffusion Model for High-Fidelity OCT-to-OCT Image Translation and Precise Anti-VEGF Therapy Response Prediction in Diabetic Macular Edema
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03958v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diabetic macular edema (DME) is a leading cause of severe vision loss among working-age adults. Although intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections currently serve as the first-line therapy for DME, a notable subset of patients fails to respond despite the substantial cost and clinical burden, suggesting they may benefit more from alternative interventions. Automated, noninvasive pre-treatment response assessment could therefore spare non-responders from the current trial-and-error treatment paradigm. In this study, we propose a novel conditional adversarial diffusion framework that synthesizes post-treatment optical coherence tomography (OCT) images from baseline scans, enabling the derivation of each patient's initial response to anti-VEGF therapy. The model was developed with subject-level 5-fold cross-validation on a US cohort (n = 127) and externally validated on an independent Iranian cohort (n = 44). Benchmarked against fourteen baseline and state-of-the-art translation models, the proposed model achieved the best treatment-response prediction performance among the methods evaluated for that task on both cohorts, with balanced accuracies of 85.7% and 93.0% on the US cohort and 85.2% and 95.3% on the external Iranian cohort at the 10% and 20% central subfield thickness reduction thresholds, respectively. Ultimately, this framework offers a decision-support tool to help ophthalmologists anticipate initial anti-VEGF outcomes in DME prior to treatment initiation, toward personalized therapy selection. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

articles.title: Evaluating the Impact of Nonlinear Registration on Longitudinal PET Analysis in a Rodent Stroke Model
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Longitudinal rodent positron emission tomography (PET) studies of stroke and neuromodulation rely on accurate registration to a common atlas space to detect group-level effects. Prior work applying ultra-high frequency low-intensity magnetic stimulation (UHF-LiMS) to a rat model of chronic capsule infarct used affine normalization to a Sprague Dawley MRI template without evaluating that choice. We compare a two-stage (affine and nonlinear) pipeline against an affine- only one for rat PET-to-atlas alignment on the same dataset. Across 32 longitudinal [18F]-FDG PET scans (8 rats, 4 timepoints), the nonlinear stage gave a higher Dice similarity coefficient on every scan, and the gain was significant at the rat level. Jacobian determinants showed no folding on the sampling grid. Group-level linear mixed-effects maps of change from baseline (AFNI 3dLME), computed identically under both pipelines, differ in the size, number and location of their suprathreshold clusters. In this dataset, the registration pipeline is therefore a variable that can change the interpretation of downstream group-level analyses.

articles.title: DUNEDepth: Bronchoscopic Depth and Pose Estimation via Hybrid Adaptation of a 3D-Vision Foundation Model
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: State-of-the-art bronchoscopy guidance systems and computer-aided diagnosis methods have emerged as important tools for early lung cancer detection. Effective use of these tools depends on being able to accurately link a patient's bronchoscopic airway exam video to their pre-operative 3D chest CT scan. Unfortunately, the derivation of such links, which include bronchoscope depth and camera motion, from the exam video remains an open problem. Building on recently proposed 3D-vision foundation models, we propose DUNEDepth, a hybrid architecture that combines a shared DUNE ViT encoder, a twin MASt3R cross-attention decoder structure, and a prediction head that includes elements of the MASt3R and Reloc3r models. To fine-tune the architecture to our application, we utilize an integrated hybrid synthetic-supervised/self-supervised training strategy that draws on both bronchoscopic video and CT-derived virtual bronchoscopic views. Experiments drawing on bronchoscopic video sequences demonstrate that DUNEDepth more accurately derives depth information and camera motion trajectories than previously proposed self-supervised methods.

articles.title: An automated photometric pipeline for measuring the corotation radius of spiral galaxies
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The corotation radius R_CR of a spiral galaxy marks the radius where the angular speed of the spiral pattern matches the orbital speed of the disk material. Despite its importance for understanding spiral structure and galaxy evolution, very few galaxies have corotation measurements, often derived using heterogeneous techniques. We present an automated photometric pipeline that identifies corotation radii by tracking the azimuthal phase offset between young and old stellar populations. Building on the color-gradient framework of \citet{Puerari1997}, we extract azimuthal brightness profiles from deprojected dual-band images, fit periodic models to the profiles, and identify corotation candidates at radii where the phase difference between the two stellar tracers changes sign. Each candidate is assigned an adaptive uncertainty interval and reported with a goodness-of-fit metric. We benchmark the method against a cross-method literature compilation, scoring every technique -- including our own -- against a reference built from the published measurements alone and evaluated leave-one-out. Over the $90$ galaxies for which such a reference exists, the pipeline places a correct corotation radius in $80.0\%$ of them, recovers $63.6\%$ of their known corotation radii, and reaches a harmonic mean of recall and purity of $0.58$, the highest values of any method in the comparison. Unlike the published methods, each of which was applied to a small, curated set of galaxies, our pipeline is run on the entire reference sample without any pre-selection, a sample two to six times larger than existing methods. articles.title: COSMIO: A Benchmark for Cross-Survey Modality Imputation
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large-scale astronomical surveys define a heterogeneous, partially observed multi-survey learning setting: each object is observed by only a subset of surveys, while survey observations differ in resolutions, wavelength coverage, noise characteristics, and footprints. This setting gives rise to a natural machine learning problem: given observations of an object in some surveys, how to infer its appearance in other surveys. We formalize this as the problem of cross-survey modality imputation and introduce COSMIO, a multi-survey benchmark of aligned observations obtained by forward-rendered shared astrophysical scenes across LSST, Euclid, and Roman under survey-specific instrument characteristics. The benchmark enables systematic evaluation of imputation across source-target survey combinations and missing-survey patterns. We evaluate a broad range of machine learning methods for imputation, which reveal a clear domain gap: methods developed for existing imputation settings transfer poorly to the survey setting. We identify rare-event imputation as a central challenge. This regime arises in the early stages of new surveys, when rare but scientifically valuable phenomena may be available only from prior surveys. We use strong gravitational lensing, where light from a background galaxy is gravitationally deflected by a foreground galaxy, as a representative rare-event setting. We evaluate model performance on zero-shot imputation of gravitational lenses and on downstream scientific tasks using the imputed lens observations. On our constructed evaluation set of galaxy-galaxy strong lenses, performance degrades under rare-event distribution shift, and this degradation further propagates to the downstream lens-detection task. articles.title: RAFT: Reasoning-Aligned Fine-Tuning Improves Robustness of VLA Post-Training
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04368v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adapting a generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policy to a target task with limited demonstrations can improve nominal task success while reducing robustness to variations in appearance, objects, and instructions. We introduce reasoning-aligned fine-tuning (RAFT), a two-stage post-training procedure: RAFT first trains low-rank adapters on task-relevant reasoning annotations, then freezes them while fine-tuning the policy on action demonstrations. On a physical DROID robot, RAFT achieves $75.0\%$ out-of-distribution success, compared with $27.9\%$ for plain fine-tuning; on a multi-stage bimanual YAM task, it reaches $70.0\%$ mean success, compared with $36.0\%$ for the strongest baseline. RAFT also improves success under visual, object, and instruction shifts in simulated pick-and-place and open-drawer tasks. Compared with plain fine-tuning, RAFT policies place more attention on annotated task regions and yield higher linear-probe accuracy for object identity in later layers. A broader reasoning-data mixture further improves downstream success across demonstration budgets.

articles.title: Hybrid Quantum--Classical Pauli-Correlator Architecture for Image Reconstruction
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the Pauli-Correlator Autoencoder (PCAE), a hybrid quantum--classical architecture for image reconstruction. PCAE splits an image into patches and compresses each patch as a matrix product state (MPS). A small quantum circuit turns each compressed patch into a few measured numbers, and a classical neural network rebuilds the patch from these numbers and the patch position. A learnable energy term, taken from physics, is added to training and tracked as training proceeds. Two versions place the six qubits on a line (PCAE1D) or on a grid (PCAE2D). An averaging step makes the PCAE2D features follow rotations and reflections of the image exactly. Trained on one image at a time, PCAE2D rebuilds images from six public datasets with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 25.8 to 41.6 decibels. On CIFAR-10 images not used in training, a formula-based stand-in for the PCAE2D features performs within 1 decibel of several simpler classical methods. Five trained models also run on real IBM quantum computers without retraining, and rebuild images at 25.90 to 31.52 decibels. A short argument and a synthetic test show that, with a linear final layer, measuring qubits in pairs is needed for targets built from products of inputs. These results show that PCAE works as a hybrid model that rebuilds varied images and runs on today's quantum hardware at the six-qubit scale.

articles.title: Hybrid Particle-Voxel Dynamics for Multimodal 3D World Simulation
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predicting how the world evolves in response to robot actions is central to policy learning, evaluation, and planning. However, many action-conditioned world models predict future observations in 2D image or video space without explicitly modeling the underlying 3D scene, making spatial consistency across viewpoints and over long-horizon interactions challenging. We introduce 3D World Simulator, an action-conditioned multimodal world modeling framework that jointly predicts appearance, geometry, and tactile observations from a unified 3D representation. Our approach combines a hybrid particle-voxel autoencoder that compresses point clouds into compact 3D voxel latents with an action-conditioned latent dynamics model that predicts their evolution. The shared 3D representation supports geometrically consistent rendering from arbitrary viewpoints and flexible integration of spatially aligned tactile signals. Our experiments demonstrate interactive, long-horizon, multimodal prediction at 50 Hz. We then show how our model enables scalable data generation for policy training and evaluation using tactile and multi-view visual observations, including wrist-mounted and novel camera views. Furthermore, we scale our method to large datasets containing diverse objects and demonstrate model-based planning with unseen objects and robot configurations. Together, these results highlight the potential of hybrid particle-voxel dynamics as a foundation for multimodal 3D world simulation.

articles.title: Sparse-View 3D Coronary Reconstruction from Vessel Segmentations Using a Diffusion Prior
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04604v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reconstructing three-dimensional (3D) coronary anatomy from sparse angiographic views could support percutaneous coronary intervention, but limited angular coverage and imperfect vessel segmentations introduce substantial geometric ambiguity. We propose a vessel-specific reconstruction framework combining a learned 3D diffusion prior, visual-hull initialization, and projection-based data consistency. The unconditional diffusion model is trained on coronary vessel masks without paired 2D--3D data and reused across different view counts without retraining. During inference, a scaled visual hull initializes reconstruction, while projection-based updates constrain diffusion refinement using patient-specific vessel observations. We evaluated the framework on simulated angiograms derived from ImageCAS computed tomography angiography volumes using two, four, and eight views at two contrast levels. Across 50 evaluation coronary-tree cases, the proposed method achieved higher mean Dice and clDice than visual hull, deep image prior (DIP), and hash-grid implicit neural representation (INR) at all view counts under reduced contrast. With eight views, improvements over DIP, the best-performing baseline at lower contrast, were approximately 0.13 in Dice and 0.22 in clDice. At higher contrast, performance remained competitive with hash-grid INR, the best-performing eight-view baseline. The preferred diffusion starting timestep depended on observation quality and view count, with excessive refinement reducing accuracy at higher contrast. Projection guidance improved both metrics across all conditions. articles.title: LIPS-PC: Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In single-pixel (ghost) imaging, known illumination patterns probe an object and a detector with no spatial resolution returns one number per pattern. Each measurement costs acquisition time and photons and, for ionizing probes, contributes to delivered dose. Motivated by automated radiographic defect screening, where a class label suffices, we introduce Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification (LIPS-PC). The patterns are learned end-to-end while the measurement operator remains one fixed linear matrix, identical for every input. We parameterize it as a residual correction to a two-dimensional discrete cosine transform (2D-DCT), $D=D_{\mathrm{base}}+\Delta$, and jointly train the correction and a compact classifier using cross-entropy, without a reconstruction objective. This yields a task-driven linear embedding through optimization. We evaluate LIPS-PC numerically on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST under a controlled protocol, then on RIAWELC, a real industrial X-ray weld-radiograph dataset. Across five budgets, $M\in{8,16,32,64,128}$, corresponding to sampling ratios from below 1% to 12.5%, the learned operator outperforms the best tested fixed transform by 9-15 percentage points at $M=8$ on all three datasets. Its eight-measurement accuracy requires roughly 16-32 measurements with the best fixed transform, indicating a $2\times$ to $4\times$ saving at comparable accuracy. The advantage generally shrinks as $M$ increases, with a small reversal on RIAWELC at higher budgets. These results show that learning what to measure is especially valuable when measurements are scarce.

articles.title: Trusting Imagined Futures: Auditing Imagined Rewards for VLA Post-Training
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04873v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video world models enable candidate actions to be evaluated through imagined outcomes, but high predicted rewards can favor trajectories with poor execution quality. We introduce Trusting Imagined Futures (TIF), an offline supervision selection method for vision-language-action (VLA) post-training that audits predicted rewards using execution feedback. A multidimensional reward model predicts a utility score for candidate ranking and five dimensions of execution quality. An auditor uses reward predictions and uncertainty to identify overestimation patterns learned from paired imagined videos and real executions. TIF accepts the candidate with the highest predicted utility when its advantage over the existing trajectory exceeds a margin and its audit risk passes a threshold; otherwise, it retains the existing supervision. The retained real trajectories then supervise behavior cloning. Across four LIBERO suites and three training seeds, TIF achieves a mean success rate of 76.25%, improving over training on the existing trajectories by 3.00 percentage points with the same trajectory count and training budget. Adding audit gating yields 1.47 percentage points with the reward model and advantage margin held fixed. The gains persist against advantage ranking and logistic regression risk selection at matched replacement counts. On recorded videos from three real robot tasks, TIF increases clean completion among selected trajectories from 58.33% to 70.00% across 60 candidate pools.

articles.title: Do Agentic Policies Need to Look at Every Step? Geometric Abstraction for Reasoning and Action
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.05058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent multimodal language models can reason directly about robot scenes, but it is unclear whether they need to repeatedly reinterpret raw visual observations at every step of an interaction. We propose shifting routine spatial reasoning from images to text and symbols through a 3D geometric abstraction that is refreshed locally from observations and read directly by the language models. Specifically, our interface represents scene geometry via typed, evidence-aware symbolic references to object parts, grounds them from calibrated RGB-D, and returns compact textual checkpoints with metric residuals after each action. Symbolic task structure can thus be reused across decisions while metric values are rebound to the current scene, with direct visual reasoning invoked only on demand. Across offline policy synthesis and continuous online execution, reasoning over grounded text and symbols improves multi-step manipulation completion while substantially reducing repeated multimodal queries, positioning explicit geometric state as an effective substrate for agentic robot policies.

articles.title: Trajectory Evaluation via Rollout-Free World Model for End-to-end Autonomous Driving
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.05072v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Although existing candidate trajectory evaluators have substantially improved end-to-end planning accuracy, their underlying mechanism remains suboptimal. Model-based evaluators typically make scoring future-aware by explicitly predicting candidate-conditioned future states over the planning horizon, which we term rollout. However, rollout incurs high inference cost and accumulates prediction errors. We argue that planning does not require reconstructing a full future scene for each candidate, but only future-relevant information for reliable comparison. We therefore propose RFWorld, a Rollout-Free World model for end-to-end trajectory evaluation. RFWorld constructs a shared scene memory and shapes it into a future-readable representation via lightweight training-time temporal readout with semantic supervision, keeping training overhead low. At inference time, candidate trajectories directly query the shared memory via sparse spatial readout for scoring, reducing computation by roughly the planning horizon times the number of candidate trajectories, while avoiding recursive rollout errors. Experiments on NAVSIM and Bench2Drive show that RFWorld learns a more planning-aligned world representation and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.05106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate segmentation of the mitral valve from three-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography (3D TEE) is severely restricted by the scarcity of publicly available expert- annotated volumetric datasets. We employed a DeepMitral residual U-Net model on the public MVSeg2023 dataset, comparing six conditions over three runs: real-only training, traditional augmentation, FDA with each generative source, and a non-AI FDA control using real-image style donors, plus an optimization-matched real-only control and a \b{eta} sensitivity analysis. Case-level paired testing showed that FDA with these generative sources led to significant reductions in boundary- and surface-related errors across all three donor conditions relative to the primary real-only baseline. However, the impact on the core segmentation metric, Generalized Dice Score (GDS), proved generator-dependent. ChatGPT-FDA showed a significant GDS advantage over the optimization-matched control but not over the primary baseline, and Gemini-FDA showed no significant GDS difference. Notably, only MAI-FDA provided a statistically robust and significant increase in GDS compared to the primary baseline. The \b{eta} sensitivity was not robust across training runs. These findings confirm that FDA remains an important augmentation mechanism. articles.title: Graph-Aggregated Prototype Learning for Remote Sensing Semantic Change Detection
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2507.10938v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Semantic change detection (SCD) extends the binary change detection task to provide not only the change locations but also the detailed "from-to" categories in multi-temporal remote sensing data. Such detailed semantic insights into changes offer considerable advantages for a wide array of applications. However, since SCD involves the simultaneous optimization of multiple tasks, the model is prone to negative transfer due to task-specific learning difficulties and conflicting gradient flows. To address this issue, we propose Graph-Aggregated Prototype Learning for Remote Sensing Semantic Change Detection(GAPL-SCD). In this framework, a multi-task joint optimization method is designed to optimize the primary task of semantic segmentation and change detection, along with the auxiliary task of graph aggregation prototype learning. Adaptive weight allocation and gradient rotation methods are used to alleviate the conflict between training tasks and improve multi-task learning capabilities. Specifically, the graph aggregation prototype learning module constructs an interaction graph using high-level features. Prototypes serve as class proxies, enabling category-level domain alignment across time points and reducing interference from irrelevant changes. Additionally, the proposed self-query multi-level feature interaction and bi-temporal feature fusion modules further enhance multi-scale feature representation, improving performance in complex scenes. Experimental results on the SECOND and Landsat-SCD datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, with significant improvements in accuracy and robustness for SCD task.

articles.title: Compact Attention: Exploiting Structured Spatio-Temporal Sparsity for Fast Video Generation
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2508.12969v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The quadratic computational complexity of self-attention mechanisms imposes a critical constraint on transformer-based video generation, particularly for synthesizing ultra-long and high-definition sequences. While most sparse attention techniques employ fixed or heuristic patterns, they often struggle to accommodate the heterogeneous and layer-specific redundancies inherent in video diffusion transformers (VDiTs). We find that different attention heads consistently concentrate most of their attention mass in different coarse query-key regions, a behavior we call functional specialization. Although individual attention values vary with the generated content, these regions remain similar across prompts and random seeds. Leveraging these insights, we introduce Compact Attention, a hardware-aware sparse attention framework for efficient long-video synthesis. We quantify this stability and use it to construct searchable, reusable, head-specific masks. Based on the observation, we propose a deformable dual-window sparse pattern mechanism that flexibly approximates local and axial attention regions within one tile-aligned mask family. To avoid manually choosing a mask for each head, we develop a recall-driven offline auto-search algorithm that identifies high-quality sparse masks while leveraging temporal stability for mask reuse. Extensive evaluations on Wan2.1 (14B) and Hunyuan-Video demonstrate that Compact Attention achieves 2.25x/3.03x attention speedups over FlashAttention-2 and 1.20x/1.74x over FlashAttention-3, respectively, while maintaining visual quality and temporal consistency comparable to full-attention baselines. articles.title: BEVTraj: Map-Free Multimodal Trajectory Prediction with Sensor-Derived BEV Context and Sparse Goal Reasoning
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2509.10080v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Trajectory prediction is a key task in autonomous driving, where a model must forecast plausible future motions of surrounding agents from dynamic histories and scene context. Many recent methods use high-definition (HD) maps to provide explicit road topology and semantic constraints, but such maps are costly to maintain, geographically limited, and difficult to update in changing environments. This paper presents Bird's-Eye View Trajectory Prediction (BEVTraj), a map-free trajectory prediction framework that directly uses BEV features constructed from raw multi-sensor data. Since sensor-derived BEV features are dense and only implicitly structured, BEVTraj employs deformable attention to selectively aggregate agent-relevant spatial context from sparse locations rather than processing the entire BEV grid uniformly. In addition, a Sparse Goal Candidate Proposal module combines overlapping mode-wise anchor clusters with attention-based goal prediction to generate compact, scene-adaptive goal hypotheses. These goals are decoded and iteratively refined into multimodal trajectories, while trajectory-aware mode scoring and temporal consistency modeling improve confidence estimation and suppress abrupt, physically implausible refinement updates. Experiments on nuScenes and Argoverse 2 Sensor show that BEVTraj achieves competitive results under a map-free setting without using pre-built HD maps, while ablation studies and qualitative analyses illustrate the roles of BEV context aggregation and sparse goal reasoning. The source code is available at https://github.com/Kongminsang/bevtraj.

articles.title: A-TPT: Angular Diversity Calibration Properties for Test-Time Prompt Tuning of Vision-Language Models
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2510.26441v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Test-time prompt tuning (TPT) has emerged as a promising technique for adapting large vision-language models (VLMs) to unseen tasks without relying on labeled data. However, the lack of dispersion between textual features can hurt calibration performance, which raises concerns about VLMs' reliability, trustworthiness, and safety. Current TPT approaches primarily focus on improving prompt calibration by either maximizing average textual feature dispersion or enforcing orthogonality constraints to encourage angular separation. However, these methods may not always have optimal angular separation between class-wise textual features, which implies overlooking the critical role of angular diversity. To address this, we propose A-TPT, a novel TPT framework that introduces angular diversity to encourage uniformity in the distribution of normalized textual features induced by corresponding learnable prompts. This uniformity is achieved by maximizing the minimum pairwise angular distance between features on the unit hypersphere. We show that our approach consistently surpasses state-of-the-art TPT methods in reducing the aggregate average calibration error while maintaining comparable accuracy through extensive experiments with various backbones on different datasets. Notably, our approach exhibits superior zero-shot calibration performance on natural distribution shifts and generalizes well to medical datasets. We provide extensive analyses, including theoretical aspects, to establish the grounding of A-TPT. These results highlight the potency of promoting angular diversity to achieve well-dispersed textual features, significantly improving VLM calibration during test-time adaptation. Our code will be made publicly available.

articles.title: WLC: Weber-Inspired Local Contrast Metric for Low-Altitude Image Fusion
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2512.15211v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Infrared and visible image fusion is a pivotal technology in low-altitude Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) reconnaissance missions, enabling robust target detection and tracking by integrating thermal saliency with environmental textures. However, the advancement of fusion algorithms is hindered by a critical evaluation bottleneck. In this paper, we identify a systematic failure in traditional no-reference metrics (specifically Statistics-based and Gradient-based metrics) within complex low-light environments, termed as ``Noise Trap''. It is mathematically proven that these metrics are positively correlated with high-frequency sensor noise, paradoxically assigning higher scores to degraded images and misguiding algorithm optimization. To resolve this dilemma, this paper proposes the Weber-inspired Local Contrast (WLC) metric. Grounded in the psychophysical principle of Weber's Law, WLC shifts the evaluation paradigm from global statistical distribution to local semantic contrast. By leveraging infrared priors, it effectively decouples target saliency from global background noise. Extensive experiments on the DroneVehicle dataset demonstrate that WLC exhibits high ``Semantic Discriminability'' in distinguishing thermal targets from background clutter. Furthermore, it achieves remarkable computational efficiency, thus, establishing itself as a reliable and real-time standard for intelligent UAV systems.

articles.title: Diffusion-DRF: Free, Rich, and Differentiable Reward for Video Diffusion Fine-Tuning
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2601.04153v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Video diffusion alignment has been heavily relied on scalar rewards. These rewards are typically derived from learned reward models in human preference datasets, requiring additional training and extensive collection. Moreover, scalar rewards provide coarse, global supervision, offering limited prompt-generation mismatch credit assignment and making models prone to reward exploitation and unstable optimization. We propose Diffusion-DRF, a free, rich, and differentiable reward framework for video diffusion fine-tuning. Diffusion-DRF employs a frozen, off-the-shelf Vision-Language Model (VLM) as the critic, eliminating the need for reward model training. Instead of relying on a single scalar reward, it decomposes each user prompt into multi-dimensional questions with freeform dense VQA explanation queries, yielding information-rich feedback. By direct differentiable optimization over this rich feedback, Diffusion-DRF achieves stable reward-based tuning without preference datasets collection. Diffusion-DRF achieves significant gains both quantitatively and qualitatively, outperforming state-of-the-art Flow-GRPO by 4.74% in overall performance on unseen VBench-2.0.

articles.title: ColorConceptBench: A Benchmark for Probabilistic Color-Concept Understanding in Text-to-Image Models
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2601.16836v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) models have advanced considerably in generating high-quality images from textual descriptions. However, their ability to associate colors with concepts remains largely constrained to explicit color names or codes, while their capacity to handle \emph{implicit concepts}, such as emotions and visual states, remains underexplored. To address this gap, we introduce ColorConceptBench, an expert-annotated benchmark that systematically evaluates color-concept associations through probabilistic color distributions. ColorConceptBench moves beyond explicit color specifications by examining how models interpret 1,281 implicit color concepts, grounded in 6,584 human annotations. Our evaluation of nine leading T2I models reveals that performance varies substantially across semantic categories, and models exhibit a significant lack of sensitivity to abstract semantics. These limitations persist even when applying classifier-free guidance scaling at inference time, suggesting that achieving human-like color understanding demands a shift in how models learn and represent implicit semantic meaning.

articles.title: Temporal Grounding of Video Large Language Model via Holistic Event Perception and Matching
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2602.05215v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite recent advances in Video Large Language Models (Vid-LLMs), Temporal Video Grounding (TVG) targeting precise localization of time segments of query events remains a grand challenge. Recent studies attempt to address this challenge by matching two separate tokens to all frame features and identifying the start and end frames of events based on the highest matching similarities. However, this approach relies heavily on the exact start and end timestamps, which are often ambiguous without capturing the semantic continuity and integrity of the event. To this end, we design E.M.Ground, a temporal grounding Vid-LLM that tackles the TVG challenge from a holistic and coherent event perception perspective. E.M.Ground introduces three novel designs: (i) It introduces a special token that aggregates information from all frames of query events with varying lengths, thereby preserving semantic continuity and integrity for accurate event matching. (ii) It introduces Savitzky-Golay smoothing to suppress the noise and abrupt changes in token-to-frame similarities across adjacent timestamps, thereby improving prediction accuracy. (iii) It aggregates multi-grained frame features to enhance the reliability of token-to-frame matching and improve temporal understanding, thereby compensating for the compression-induced information loss. Extensive experiments on widely adopted TVG benchmarks, along with in-depth analyses, demonstrate that E.M.Ground achieves strong overall performance, with the most pronounced improvements on single-event grounding and boundary-integrity tasks.

articles.title: TFusionOcc: T-Primitive Based Object-Centric Multi-Sensor Fusion Framework for 3D Occupancy Prediction
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2602.06400v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The prediction of 3D semantic occupancy enables autonomous vehicles (AVs) to perceive the fine-grained geometric and semantic scene structure for safe navigation and decision-making. Existing methods mainly rely on either voxel-based representations, which incur redundant computation over empty regions, or object-centric Gaussian primitives, whose ellipsoidal per-primitive geometry can limit representation efficiency for complex, non-convex, and asymmetric structures under a fixed primitive and computational budget. In this paper, we present TFusionOcc, a T-primitive-based object-centric multi-sensor fusion framework for 3D semantic occupancy prediction. Specifically, we introduce a family of Student's t-distribution-based T-primitives, including the plain T-primitive, T-Superquadric, and deformable T-Superquadric with inverse warping, where the deformable T-Superquadric serves as the key geometry-enhancing primitive. We further develop a unified probabilistic formulation based on the Student's t-distribution and the T-mixture model (TMM) to jointly model occupancy and semantics, and design a tightly coupled multi-stage fusion architecture to integrate camera and LiDAR cues effectively. Extensive experiments on nuScenes demonstrate competitive performance against recent state-of-the-art methods and strong performance among object-centric multi-sensor approaches, while additional evaluations on nuScenes-C show robust performance across most corruption scenarios. Further evaluation on the separate SemanticKITTI benchmark demonstrates cross-dataset applicability. The code will be available at: https://github.com/DanielMing123/TFusionOcc

articles.title: VidVec: Unlocking Video MLLM Embeddings for Video-Text Retrieval
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2602.08099v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent studies have adapted generative Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) into embedding extractors for text-vision tasks, typically by fine-tuning them to produce universal representations. However, their performance on video-text retrieval often remains below that of dedicated Video Foundation Models. In this paper, we revisit the video-text retrieval capabilities of MLLMs. We first analyze the zero-shot retrieval capabilities of pretrained MLLMs and show that they already encode substantial retrieval-relevant information: combining intermediate-layer embeddings with a calibrated MLLM head yields strong performance without any training. To further exploit these capabilities, we introduce a lightweight text-based optimization strategy that requires no paired multimodal data. Our method uses dense video captions as rich textual surrogates for video semantics and short summaries as compact, query-like views, showing that a carefully designed text-alignment objective can improve multimodal alignment through the shared MLLM backbone. We backup these findings through in-depth analysis. Remarkably, our lightweight text-only optimization outperforms its counterpart trained with paired video-text supervision, which is substantially more computationally expensive. Furthermore, our method outperforms existing approaches, often by a substantial margin, and achieves state-of-the-art performance across common video-text retrieval benchmarks. More broadly, our findings highlight the untapped retrieval capabilities of pretrained MLLMs and establish text-only optimization as a more efficient and effective substitute for large-scale visual supervision.

articles.title: Evaluation of Visual Processing Should Be Human-Centered, Not Metric-Centered
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2603.00643v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This position paper argues that the evaluation of modern visual processing systems should no longer be driven primarily by single-metric image quality assessment benchmarks, particularly in the era of generative and perception-oriented methods. Image restoration exemplifies this divergence: while objective IQA metrics enable reproducible, scalable evaluation, they have increasingly drifted apart from human perception and user preferences. We contend that this mismatch risks constraining innovation and misguiding research progress across visual processing tasks. Rather than rejecting metrics altogether, this paper calls for a rebalancing of evaluation paradigms, advocating a more human-centered, context-aware, and fine-grained approach to assessing the visual models' outcomes.

articles.title: EmbedTalk: Talking Head Synthesis using Gaussian Embeddings
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2603.07604v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a popular method for real-time talking head synthesis, offering high-quality renderings at low latency. Tri-planes are a common choice for encoding Gaussians prior to deformation since they provide a compact and continuous representation. However, tri-plane encodings are limited by grid resolution and approximation errors introduced by projecting 3D volumetric fields onto 2D subspaces. Recent work has demonstrated the effectiveness of per-Gaussian embeddings for driving temporal deformations in 4D scene reconstruction. We introduce EmbedTalk, which leverages these embeddings to model speech-driven facial deformations for talking head synthesis. Comprehensive experiments show that EmbedTalk improves rendering quality, lip synchronisation, and motion consistency over previous 3DGS-based methods, while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art generative models. Replacing tri-plane features with embeddings also yields significantly more compact models that achieve 60+ FPS on a laptop GPU (RTX 2060 6 GB). Code and further details are available at https://arpita2512.github.io/EmbedTalk/

articles.title: FlatLands: Indoor floormap completion from a single egocentric view
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2603.16016v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A single egocentric image typically captures only a small portion of the floor, yet a complete metric traversability map of the surroundings would better serve applications such as indoor navigation. We introduce FlatLands, a dataset and benchmark for single-view indoor floor-map completion in metric bird's-eye view (BEV), evaluating eleven models: both deterministic and generative. FlatLands contain 270,575 observations from 17,656 scene records across six metric 3D datasets, with aligned observation, visibility, validity, and ground-truth maps and both in- and out-of-distribution protocols. We compare training-free, deterministic, ensemble, and generative methods on shared geometry-derived inputs and, without fine-tuning, on maps estimated from real egocentric RGB images. Our results show that predicting floor almost everywhere can achieve high IoU when most evaluated cells are floor, while generative sample sets outperform the best single-output model under a proper scoring rule and support safer risk-weighted planning. FlatLands establishes a rigorous testbed for evaluating both floor-map accuracy and how effectively alternative completions represent the ambiguity of unseen space.

articles.title: To See or To Please: Uncovering Visual Sycophancy and Split Beliefs in VLMs
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2603.18373v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When Vision-Language Models (VLMs) answer correctly, do they rely on the image? We introduce a Tri-Layer Diagnostic Framework that asks three questions of every (image, question) pair when the image is blanked: does the model register that the image is missing (Latent Anomaly Detection, LAD), does its output distribution depend on the image (Visual Necessity Score, VNS), and does it nonetheless commit to a content answer? The cascade assigns each pair of any existing benchmark to one of four modes: Perceptual Blindness, Language Shortcut, Visual Sycophancy (the blank image registers and matters, yet the model commits to a fabricated answer), or Robust Refusal. Across nine open-weight VLMs and 9,000 model-sample pairs, 28.1% are Visual Sycophancy, 18.6% Language Shortcut, 5.6% Perceptual Blindness, and 47.8% Robust Refusal. The modes are strongly model-specific: the Qwen3-VL models refuse on blank input in 93-98% of pairs, whereas Pixtral-12B commits to an answer in 72%. Within-generation scaling increases Visual Sycophancy in both Qwen2.5-VL (7B->72B: 25.5->40.1%) and Llama-3.2-Vision (11B->90B: 34.3->48.0%), while the newer Qwen3-VL generation nearly eliminates it. A blinded human study confirms that LAD and VNS track what annotators observe, and that 80% of Visual-Sycophancy responses carry no textual sign that the image was blank.

articles.title: JDCNet Uses Confidence Gated Privileged Modality Distillation for Cost Preserving X Ray Inference
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2603.29167v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Training-only privileged-modality learning uses an expensive modality during training while keeping a single-modality deployment path. We study chest radiograph (X-ray) classification with same-patient computed tomography (CT) available only during training. JDCNet adds an auxiliary CT-teacher target, the teacher's argmax label or its softmax distribution through a Kullback--Leibler term (soft-KL), only on samples whose teacher confidence exceeds a threshold; the deployed model has the same ResNet-18 computation graph as the supervised baseline. On 510 same-patient pairs from the public BIMCV-COVID19 releases of the Valencian Region Medical ImageBank (113 COVID-19, 397 non-COVID), with patient-level five-fold cross-validation and three seeds, 15 of 16 adaptively explored JDCNet configurations improved mean balanced accuracy (BA) over the supervised baseline (average $+0.020$), but none remained significant after Holm adjustment. In a pre-registered experiment with 240 batch-matched supervised restarts on the same splits, batch size had no detectable effect on the baseline (BA $0.620$ versus $0.625$), and when both methods selected one of 16 runs per cell on the validation partition, JDCNet exceeded supervised training by $+0.037$ BA (95\% confidence interval $+0.016$ to $+0.058$; patient-level $+0.007$ to $+0.068$). Logit distillation and contrastive alignment did not help. Teacher diagnostics indicate that the gate acts mainly as CT-informed sample weighting. All models, including JDCNet, performed at chance on an external radiograph set. Confidence-gated CT supervision thus gives a small within-cohort advantage on one public cohort and a binary task; generalization requires independent paired replication.

articles.title: Query-Conditioned Evidential Keyframe Sampling for MLLM-Based Long-Form Video Understanding
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2604.01002v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown strong performance on video question answering, but their application to long-form videos is constrained by limited context length and computational cost, making keyframe sampling essential. Existing approaches typically rely on semantic relevance or reinforcement learning, which either fail to capture evidential clues or suffer from inefficient combinatorial optimization. In this work, we propose an evidence-driven keyframe sampling framework motivated by an information-theoretic perspective. We consider maximizing the conditional mutual information between the selected frames and the answer given the query as an idealized objective, and use a modular singleton-gain surrogate to motivate a tractable frame-wise selection criterion. Guided by this motivation, we train a query-conditioned evidence scoring network using annotated answer-supporting segments. A contrastive objective encourages greater aggregate score mass on frames from evidence regions than on background frames, providing a practical evidence-based criterion beyond semantic similarity. Experiments on long-form video understanding benchmarks show that our method consistently outperforms prior sampling strategies under comparable frame budgets. With Qwen2.5-VL-7B under the same 32-frame budget, our method improves over uniform sampling by 10.1 points on LVBench and 4.4 points on the long-video subset of VideoMME.

articles.title: VideoZeroBench: Probing the Limits of Video MLLMs with Spatio-Temporal Evidence Verification
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2604.01569v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Video multimodal large language models achieve strong results on existing benchmarks, but answer accuracy alone does not establish whether they can locate the evidence needed to answer a question. We introduce VideoZeroBench, a challenging long-video benchmark with manually annotated question-answer pairs spanning 13 video domains. Questions target fine-grained cues, fleeting events, and evidence distributed across multiple segments. Temporal intervals and key-frame boxes are annotated where applicable. All questions undergo two rounds of cross-verification for answer validity and evidence quality. Our five-level diagnostic protocol compares answering with and without evidence hints, then combines answer correctness with independently evaluated temporal and spatial grounding. Across 19 evaluated models, the best standard QA accuracy is 24.8% (Level-3), achieved by Gemini-3.7-Flash. No model exceeds 1.8% when correct answers and accurate spatio-temporal localization are jointly required (Level-5). Analyses of atomic abilities, evidence spans, input modalities, and thinking-with-videos inference further characterize where the evaluated systems struggle. These findings motivate more precise evidence search and localization for long-video question answering. Our code and data are publicly released.

articles.title: Adaptive Local Frequency Filtering for Fourier-Encoded Implicit Neural Representations
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2604.02846v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) commonly employ Fourier features to alleviate spectral bias and represent high-frequency signals. Fourier encodings, however, use the same frequency representation across spatial locations despite the spatially varying frequency content of natural signals. We propose Adaptive Frequency Implicit Neural Representation (AFINR), a spatially adaptive frequency-conditioning framework for Fourier encoded INRs. A sampling compatible Fourier dictionary first defines the explicit frequency support, and a learnable spatial control field then modulates the admitted Fourier components before decoding. The control field is parameterized in the discrete cosine transform (DCT) domain to provide a compact and continuously queryable spatial representation. AFINR can be combined with different coordinate decoders, including ReLU, SIREN, CAFE, and CAFE+. Experiments on Kodak and DIV2K show consistent average improvements across these decoder families. In particular, AFINR-CAFE+ improves CAFE+ by 3.95 dB on Kodak and 3.50 dB on DIV2K. Ablation studies characterize the effects of adaptive-field parameterization, DCT coefficient retention, and frequency-response parameters, while learned spatial responses show position-dependent use of the admitted Fourier components.

articles.title: HumanScore: Benchmarking Human Motions in Generated Videos
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2604.20157v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent advances in model architectures, compute, and data scale have driven rapid progress in video generation, producing increasingly realistic content. Yet, no prior method systematically measures how faithfully these systems render human bodies and motion dynamics. In this paper, we present HumanScore, a systematic framework to evaluate the quality of human motions in AI-generated videos. HumanScore defines six interpretable metrics spanning kinematic plausibility, temporal stability, and biomechanical consistency, enabling fine-grained diagnosis beyond visual realism alone. Through carefully designed prompts, we elicit a diverse set of movements at varying intensities and evaluate videos generated by thirteen state-of-the-art models. Our analysis reveals consistent gaps between perceptual plausibility and motion biomechanical fidelity, identifies recurrent failure modes (e.g., temporal jitter, anatomically implausible poses, and motion drift), and produces robust model rankings from quantitative and physically meaningful criteria.

articles.title: Railway Artificial Intelligence Learning Benchmark (RAIL-BENCH): A Benchmark Suite for Perception in the Railway Domain
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2604.22507v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Benchmark suites are crucial for advancing computer vision research, providing not only curated datasets but also standardized evaluation protocols for reproducible comparison. The railway domain lacks such resources, hindering progress in automated train operation. To address this gap, we present RAIL-BENCH, the first perception benchmark suite designed specifically for railways. RAIL-BENCH comprises five challenges - rail track detection, object detection, vegetation segmentation, multi-object tracking, and monocular visual odometry - each tailored to railway-specific characteristics and including a curated dataset from diverse real-world scenarios, evaluation metrics, and public scoreboards; we demonstrate the first three challenges in this paper. We further introduce LineAP, a novel segment-based average precision metric for rail track detection that decouples geometric accuracy from instance-level grouping and employs a track-width-based distance threshold approximating a fixed real-world distance, addressing key limitations of existing line detection metrics. Our benchmark suite is publicly available at https://www.mrt.kit.edu/railbench/.

articles.title: CurEvo: Curriculum-Guided Self-Evolution for Video Understanding
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2604.26707v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent self-evolution frameworks for video understanding have demonstrated the potential for autonomous improvement from unlabeled videos. However, existing approaches often suffer from weakly controlled optimization and capability progression because they lack structured guidance for generating, evaluating, and reusing supervision throughout the iterative learning process. We present CurEvo, a curriculum-guided self-evolution framework that organizes this loop as a competence-aware progression. Curriculum-Guided Self-Evolution maintains a competence-aware curriculum state and cumulative training pool across iterations. Within this loop, Multi-Dimensional Question Generation supplies complementary supervision, from directly verifiable structural questions for perception to type-conditioned questions for recognition and understanding. Type-Adaptive Evaluation separately assesses question quality and answer reliability with criteria matched to each type's evidence; its scores determine which pairs enter the pool and how the next curriculum state is updated. Across seven backbones and four VideoQA benchmarks, CurEvo consistently improves benchmark accuracy and benchmark semantic score. For Qwen2.5-VL(7B), accuracy rises from 67.84% to 69.91% on ActivityNet-QA and from 76.94% to 79.61% on NExT-QA. CurEvo thus establishes self-generated supervision as a stable route to autonomous video understanding without task-specific human QA annotations during self-evolution.

articles.title: Identity-Consistent Multi-Pose Generation of Contactless Fingerprints
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2605.03830v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Contactless fingerprint recognition has gained increasing attention due to its advantages in hygiene and acquisition flexibility. However, the absence of physical contact constraints introduces severe nonlinear geometric distortions caused by free finger poses in 3D space, resulting in a substantial cross-modal domain gap between contactless and conventional contact-based fingerprints. Existing solutions largely rely on explicit geometric correction or image enhancement, which are fragile under extreme pose variations. In this paper, we propose Identity-Consistent Multi-Pose Generation of Contactless Fingerprints (IMPOSE), a physics-inspired framework that synthesizes identity-preserving, multi-pose contactless fingerprint samples to empower recognition models. IMPOSE consists of three stages: (1) rolled fingerprint identity generation via latent diffusion with discrete codebook representations, (2) cross-modal translation from rolled to contactless modality guided by Sauvola-based local adaptive binarization as an identity anchor, and (3) physics-based multi-pose simulation through 3D finger model texture mapping and projection. The generated samples maintain strict identity consistency at the ridge topology level and spatial alignment with standard fingerprint coordinate space. Extensive experiments on the UWA and PolyU CL2CB databases demonstrate that fine-tuning fixed-length dense descriptors (FDD) with IMPOSE-synthesized data achieves state-of-the-art cross-modal matching, reducing EER to 8.74% on UWA and 2.26% on PolyU CL2CB. articles.title: OphEdit: Training-Free Text-Guided Editing of Ophthalmic Surgical Videos
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2605.07695v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-fidelity surgical video generation holds great promise for medical training and AI development, yet precise, controllable editing of such videos remains a formidable challenge. Modifying surgical attributes such as instrument, tissue interactions or procedural phases is particularly difficult due to the strict anatomical and temporal constraints of ophthalmic procedures. We introduce OphEdit, the first training-free framework for text-guided editing of ophthalmic surgical videos. Our approach uses a deterministic second-order ODE inversion pipeline to capture attention Value tensors from the source video and selectively injects them into the conditional branch of classifier-free guidance during denoising, preserving the intricate anatomical geometry of the eye while mapping text-driven semantic modifications onto the video. Clinical evaluation by an ophthalmologist shows that OphEdit handles complex transformations, such as instrument swaps and procedural variations, with superior structural fidelity and temporal consistency compared to adapted general-domain video editors, offering a scalable route to diverse surgical training data. The code and prompts can be accessed at https://github.com/ophedit/OphEdit

articles.title: Supersampling Stable Diffusion and Beyond: Training-Free Neural Network Scaling via Signal Interpolation
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2605.08698v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work presents a training-free approach for interpolating neural networks using signal interpolation methods (i.e., linear, bilinear, bicubic). We discovered this phenomenon while attempting to interpolate the convolution layers of Stable-Diffusion-1.5 for beyond-training-resolution (BTR) image generation. As we know, for generating BTR images using DDPMs (Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models), there are mainly two approaches, namely, 1) patch-wise diffusion and 2) convolution-kernel dilation. Patch-wise diffusion cannot solve the object-duplication problem efficiently, while the kernel dilation approach may be harder to fine-tune later. Thus, we proposed convolution-kernel interpolation of the Stable Diffusion 1.5 model for $4\times$ BTR image generation. We discover and show mathematically that signal interpolation methods can correctly scale convolution kernels when multiplied by a flat-attenuation factor, while achieving competitive performance against the state of the art. We then applied the same methodology to non-DDPM deep neural network architectures, adapting them for BTR image classification, achieving a worst-case performance drop of $\sim 7\%$ on the ImageNet-1k validation set. Again, we subsample the penultimate fully connected layer of VGG-16 using our method, reducing up to $\sim 9\%$ parameters with $\sim 5\%$ loss in performance. Finally, we also discuss how we can reduce the memory footprint of training neural networks to $4\times$ or greater.

articles.title: H2G: Hierarchy-Aware Hyperbolic Grouping for 3D Scenes
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2605.11967v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hierarchical 3D grouping aims to recover scene groups across multiple granularities, from fine object parts to complete objects, without relying on semantic labels or a fixed vocabulary. The main challenge is to transform 2D foundation-model cues into coherent hierarchy supervision and embed that hierarchy in a 3D representation. We propose H2G, a hyperbolic affinity field for hierarchical 3D grouping. Our method derives semantically organized tree supervision by interpreting foundation-model affinities through Dasgupta's objective for similarity-based hierarchical clustering. This supervision is distilled into a single Lorentz hyperbolic feature field, whose geometry is well suited for tree-like branching structures. A hierarchy-aware objective aligns the field with fine-level assignments, coarse object structure, compact feature clusters, and LCA (Lowest Common Ancestor) ordering. This formulation represents multiple grouping levels in one feature space, enabling semantic hierarchical grouping grounded in 2D foundation-model knowledge. Code is available at https://github.com/Rhqo/H2G.

articles.title: G$^2$TR: Generation-Guided Visual Token Reduction for Separate-Encoder Unified Multimodal Models
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2605.12309v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The development of separate-encoder Unified multimodal models (UMMs) comes with a rapidly growing inference cost due to dense visual token processing. In this paper, we focus on understanding-side visual token reduction for improving the efficiency of separate-encoder UMMs. While this topic has been widely studied for MLLMs, existing methods typically rely on attention scores, text-image similarity and so on, implicitly assuming that the final objective is discriminative reasoning. This assumption does not hold for UMMs, where understanding-side visual tokens must also preserve the model's capabilities for editing images. We propose G$^2$TR, a generation-guided visual token reduction framework for separate-encoder UMMs. Our key insight is that the generation branch provides a task-agnostic signal for identifying understanding-side visual tokens that are not only semantically relevant but also important for latent-space image reconstruction and generation. G$^2$TR estimates token importance from consistency with VAE latent, performs balanced token selection, and merges redundant tokens into retained representatives to reduce information loss. The method is training-free, plug-and-play, and applied only after the understanding encoding stage, making it compatible with existing UMM inference pipelines. Experiments on image understanding and editing benchmarks show that G$^2$TR substantially reduces visual tokens and prefill computation by 1.94x while maintaining both reasoning accuracy and editing quality, outperforming baselines on almost all benchmarks. Code is at: https://github.com/lijunxian111/G2TR.

articles.title: Cracks in the Foundation: A Civil Infrastructure Dataset to Challenge Vision Foundation Models
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2605.18413v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Automated structural health monitoring is essential to prevent catastrophic infrastructure failures. Precise, pixel-level defect segmentation is needed to accurately assess structural integrity, but progress in defect segmentation for civil infrastructures has been held back by an extreme scarcity of data, which requires costly expert annotation. The need for data is accentuated by algorithmic hurdles intrinsic to the problem, including center-bias and the need to rely more on shape when inspecting nearly textureless building materials. To remove the bottleneck, we introduce Cracks in the Foundation (CiF), the largest and most detailed civil infrastructure (instance) segmentation dataset to date, comprising $\approx$150,000 high-resolution tiles meticulously curated over five years in collaboration with civil engineering experts. With the help of this unprecedented data source, we expose a blind spot of current visual AI: despite the advent of promptable Foundation Models (FMs) and Vision Language Models (VLMs), and despite the impressive abilities of today's specialised segmentation models, it turns out that dense image understanding in the built environment is nowhere near solved. Our evaluations indicate that even the most recent zero-shot FMs face significant challenges when deployed on real-world infrastructure and even the performance of specialised models with domain-specific supervision plateaus at $\approx$25\% mAP. CiF establishes inspection of civil infrastructure, an elementary and seemingly easy perceptual task, as an open challenge that reveals fundamental weaknesses of present-day models trained predominantly on internet images, literally and figuratively highlighting cracks in the current foundation mod

articles.title: Distill to Think, Foresee to Act: Cognitive-Physical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2605.21139v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Current end-to-end autonomous driving models are fundamentally constrained by the behavioral cloning ceiling of imitation learning. While reinforcement learning offers a path to smarter autonomy, it demands two missing pieces of infrastructure: (1) a cognitive foundation that understands traffic semantics and driving intent, and (2) a foresighted physical environment that can anticipate the consequences of candidate actions. To this end, we propose CoPhy, a CognitivePhysical reinforcement learning framework for autonomous driving. To distill to think, we distill VLM knowledge into the BEV encoder and then discard the VLM entirely, retaining cognitive ability at zero inference cost while releasing the cognitive channel as a pluggable interface for optional human language commands. To foresee to act, we build an auto-regressive BEV world model that explicitly predicts future semantic maps conditioned on candidate actions, serving as an interpretable physical sandbox from which safety metrics are directly derived. Built upon this dual infrastructure, we optimize the driving policy via GRPO with a novel dual-reward mechanism: a physical reward derived from BEV rollouts enforces hard safety constraints, while a cognitive reward from a language-aligned scorer ensures intent compliance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoPhy not only achieves state-of-the-art results on NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks, but also enables safer driving via cognitively informed scene compliance and flexible intent control through user-defined language instructions. Project page: https://wuyang98.github.io/CoPhy/.

articles.title: COCOTree: A Dataset and Benchmark for Open Tree-Structured Visual Decomposition
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2605.22068v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formalize and enable the task of open tree decomposition, which segments an image into hierarchical trees of visual components with unconstrained granularity and flexibility. Specifically, we provide the foundation benchmark for this new paradigm with the following three key contributions. First, we overcome the prohibitively high cognitive and physical bottlenecks of manual annotation by developing a fully automated generation pipeline that synergizes the semantic reasoning of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) with the precise geometric grounding of SAM 3. Second, leveraging this pipeline, we construct COCOTree, a massive-scale benchmark featuring over 21K images and 1.8M structural nodes. By embracing an open-vocabulary space of over 3.5K unique labels, it successfully captures the long-tail distribution of complex physical assemblies. Notably, rigorous human evaluation confirms our generated annotations demonstrate strong alignment with human structural judgment. Third, we establish a standardized evaluation protocol by proposing the Open Tree Quality (OTQ) metric, which jointly assesses mask precision, label accuracy, and structural consistency. We release our dataset and benchmark code at https://github.com/melonkick3090/COCOTree.
